lesson.title: Net Rusher: Feet or Over Them
lesson.hook: They charge the net, and you try to blast it past them, straight onto their racquet.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time they come in, check how close they got: service line, aim at their feet; right on the net, lob.

pro.label: The net player starts favourite
pro.moment: Nuno Borges won 72.3% of his net points in 2025, joint best on tour: "When a guy comes to the net, he still has more than a 50 per cent chance of winning the point."
pro.read: You don't need a winner. Make the volley hard.

drill.name: Feet or over
drill.how: Your partner comes in and stops wherever they like. Around the service line, you must dip it at their feet. Close to the net, you must lob. The wrong choice loses the point, even if it wins.

lesson.cue: Service line, feet. On the net, over.

steps.name: They close to the service line
steps.sit: They approach and come in. They stop just inside the service line as you hit.
steps.q: Where do you send this one?
opts: Flat and deep down the line
steps.payoff: At their feet, they have to hit up, and the next ball is yours.
steps.principle: Against a net player, height matters more than pace.
steps.why: A hard ball at volley height is easy to punch away. A dipping ball makes them hit up from their shoelaces, and it floats back.
steps.take: They're at the service line? Dip it at their feet.

lines.A: Hard, but at volley height — they punch it into your open court.
lines.B: Not close enough to lob — they step back and smash it.
lines.C: They have to volley up from their feet — you pass the floater.
lines.D: Low and flat at the line — it sails long.

steps.name: They crowd the net
steps.sit: Same approach, but this time they rush right in and crowd the net.
opts: Flat and deep down the line
steps.payoff: They came too close to cover the lob.
steps.principle: The closer they come, the more the lob is on.
steps.why: Right on top of the net, your dip hasn't dropped yet when it reaches them. The topspin lob goes over their reach, and they can't get back in time.
steps.take: They're right on the net? Lob over them.

lines.A: That close, the dip is still at volley height — volleyed away.
lines.B: Right on the net, they reach it — volleyed away.
lines.C: Low and flat at the line — it sails long.
lines.D: Over them — they can't turn and run it down.

steps.name: Backhand, service line
steps.sit: Now their approach comes to your backhand. Again they stop just inside the service line.
steps.q: Which shot beats them this time?
opts: Flat and deep down the line
steps.payoff: Same read on the backhand: at the service line, aim at their feet.
steps.principle: Read where they stop, not which wing you're on.
steps.why: They stopped at the same distance as before, so the same shot works: a dipping ball they have to lift.
steps.take: Either wing: service line, feet; right on the net, lob.

lines.A: They volley up from their feet — you pass the floater.
lines.B: Hard, at volley height — they punch it away.
lines.C: Not close enough — they step back and smash it.
lines.D: Low and flat at the line — it sails long.
